thread:
Paula Mendes: hey all — quick alignment Q on the post-incident summary SLA before we lock the doc. in the draft we’ve got “within 3 business days for Sev1/Sev0”.

Paula Mendes: what do we do if we have mitigations in place but the “final fix” is still in progress / waiting on upstream / needs a longer rollout? do we still publish a summary at T+3bd?

Marissa Cole: +1, also want to avoid summaries that read like “we don’t know yet” or set wrong expectations.

Rafael Mendes: we should still publish something. customers are asking for *timeline + what happened + what we did to restore service* even if the long-term corrective action isn’t fully shipped.

Rafael Mendes: would frame it as “post-incident summary (initial)” w/ clear “follow-ups” section.

Sean Gallagher: agree. the incident is “resolved” from customer-impact POV once impact is over. the internal postmortem can keep running for longer.

Sean Gallagher: we can do: publish within 3bd with (a) impact/timeline (b) root cause category at least (c) mitigations in place (d) prevention items, marked as “in progress” where needed.

Paula Mendes: ok so SLA applies to publishing a customer summary once customer impact ends, not when the final code change lands.

Rafael Mendes: yep. otherwise we’ll miss the window on all the gnarly ones.

Dev Patel: from Support side: even a “we mitigated by X and are rolling out Y over the next week” is massively helpful. the worst is silence + customers filling in their own story.

Marissa Cole: what about wording like: “We implemented mitigations that restored service at <time>. A permanent fix is in progress; we will update this summary once complete.”

Sean Gallagher: + include “Next steps” with owner team (generic) + expected timeframe *if we can*.

Sean Gallagher: but careful with dates if we’re not sure. we can do “over the coming days” vs “by Friday”.

Paula Mendes: makes sense. do we want 1) single summary doc that can be updated, or 2) initial summary + separate follow-up post?

Elliot Price: docs POV: easier for customers if it’s one permalink. add “Last updated <date>” line + “Update” section appended when long-term fix ships.

Elliot Price: otherwise they’ll miss the follow-up unless they’re subscribed.

Rafael Mendes: +1 single permalink, treat as living summary but keep change log minimal.

Marissa Cole: as long as we don’t keep “editing history” in a way that changes what we previously claimed.

Talia Benson: proposal: standard sections:
- Summary
- Customer impact
- Timeline (UTC)
- Root cause (category + short)
- Mitigations / Remediation (what restored service)
- Prevention / Follow-ups (in progress)
- Updates (optional; if we materially learn more / ship permanent fix)

Talia Benson: and SLA: initial version within 3 business days for Sev0/Sev1. (Sev2 optional / best effort)

Paula Mendes: love it. question: can we include “root cause” if we’re still uncertain? sometimes we only have a suspected cause at T+48h.

Sean Gallagher: we can do “Preliminary cause” language, but only if we’re comfortable it won’t reverse.

Rafael Mendes: maybe we use a controlled taxonomy: “capacity exhaustion”, “dependency/provider degradation”, “release regression”, “networking”, etc. less likely to be wrong than a super specific explanation.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: +1 on categories. also: avoid including details that look like an exploit path or vendor-specific incident IDs. if dependency-related, “a third-party cloud dependency” is usually enough.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: if we *don’t know*, explicitly say “We are still investigating the underlying cause. We will update this summary when confirmed.” that’s better than guessing.

Paula Mendes: ok so requirement becomes: include root cause category when confirmed; otherwise “under investigation” + commit to updating.

Dev Patel: can we add a line like “Customer actions: none required” vs “retry / backoff / switch region” even in the summary? support gets asked that after the fact too.

Marissa Cole: in summary, maybe “Customer guidance” section only if there’s anything actionable / lingering config changes.

Rafael Mendes: yeah, but careful: don’t recommend changing config after incident unless it’s still relevant (e.g. “if you pinned us-east, consider multi-region”).

Talia Benson: action items:
- I’ll update the Confluence template to clarify: publish initial summary within 3bd after customer impact ends, even if long-term fix ongoing.
- Add “Updates” section for later permanent fix notes.
- Add allowed root-cause category list + uncertainty language.

Paula Mendes: 👍 I’ll reflect this in the PRD and call out “initial summary” vs “final fix shipped”.

Elliot Price: once updated, I’ll also tweak the public-facing “what to expect” doc to set expectations: summaries may be updated as investigations complete.

Sean Gallagher: sounds good. also let’s align the incident-bot reminder job to this: reminder at T+1bd and T+3bd post-resolve.

Rafael Mendes: + if we’re blocked on Security review for wording, we still should publish a minimal impact/timeline summary in the SLA window.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: agree — we can always ship minimal + safe, then iterate.

Paula Mendes: cool, thanks all. closing the loop once the template changes are in.
